description: We are a student team working on the Space Mission Design Game challenge for NASA Space Apps 2026.
summary: Space Mission Design Game is a browser-based educational prototype that turns mission planning into playable trade-offs. Players choose a science objective, spacecraft bus, instruments, launch vehicle and orbit while tracking budget, power, mass and data capacity. A rotatable 3D assembly shows the selected parts. A simplified launch laboratory lets players explore propellant, thrust and battery choices before piloting a mission, handling events and holding SCAN over target zones to earn science. The final report explains successes, failures and resource use. NASA/JPL Horizons positions and historical NASA imagery connect the visualization to real sources while keeping the simulated engineering and gameplay clearly labeled. Our goal is to make competing demands of space-mission design easier to understand through experimentation, not to predict real spacecraft performance.
details: Download the project ZIP, extract all files together, then open index.html in a recent desktop browser. README includes a local-server fallback if local files are restricted. No account or build step is required.The team supplied the game idea and directed the 3D gameplay and UI. AI assistance helped research, code, explain implementation, debug and test. Countdown speech is labeled AI-generated. Players choose an objective, bus, instruments, rocket and orbit. Gates check budget, mass, power and storage. A rotatable assembly updates with choices. Flight adds steering, events, SCAN and a final report. NASA positions and historical Earth/Mars imagery inform the visuals. Engineering values and prices are simplified, not flight predictions. HTML/CSS/JavaScript and Three.js support this prototype.
